newsitem.title: USA: Yellow sets changes in freight operations.
newsitem.headline: Yellow sets changes in freight operations.

text.p: Yellow Freight System, a unit of Yellow Corp, said it planned operational changes that could result in relocations or job changes for more than 1,000 employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters.
The company said it completed a review of the changes with the union in hearings held March 5 in St. Louis.
Yellow will implement major components of the plan on April 13. The changes includes more reliance on linehaul sleeper teams and increased use of intermodal rail service to move freight.

The plan calls for the company to haul almost 27 percent of all intercity freight by rail instead of linehaul trucks. A maximum of 28 percent was allowed under the 1994 National Master Freight Agreement with the Teamsters.

"This change gives us the cost and mode flexibility required to deliver the service our customers expect," said Yellow Freight President Bill Zollars. "Among other things, we will see a substantial increase in direct load shipments, which will improve on-time reliability and transit times. It also will reduce cargo claims."
The change of operations helps complete a major restructuring that aligns the company into five business groups, each with greater authority to develop and offer customized services to customers.
